A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiCoFlex, and their methods, experiments, equations, figures and appendices can be matched reliably. All supplied pages are readable. The reference to a nonexistent Appendix E.2 in v2 is an internal documentation gap, not an extraction failure.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C/G report original benchmark comparisons, runtime measurements, architecture comparisons and actionability experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds Adult sparsity sensitivity results, counterfactual variability estimates and German Credit evaluation results.

M1.justification: Both versions train a conditional MAF using target-class nearest neighbors, with sparsity parameter p and actionability mask m. Objective (4) and Algorithm 1 are retained. Removing the motivational scoring formula, renaming s-DiCoFlex and explaining context-vector construction do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix I.4 adds German Credit, described as 1,000 samples, 20 features and a binary target. The five original benchmark datasets remain. This extends coverage within the existing tabular credit-decision domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CCHVAE, DiCE, ReViSE, TABCF and Wachter; the added German Credit comparison uses the same baselines. The architecture comparison also retains MAF, NICE, RealNVP and KDE, moving from v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 5.

E3.justification: The added Adult sensitivity experiment evaluates p values 0.01, 0.08, 0.25, 1 and 2, extending the previous endpoint comparison. Existing metrics and the procedure of generating up to 100 candidates and selecting 10 valid counterfactuals remain unchanged. Newly disclosed training settings do not establish revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Section 4.7/Table 3 extends the existing sparsity analysis with intermediate p values. Appendix E.1 additionally reports qualitative sensitivity to neighbor count, actionability penalty and model capacity, but its promised quantitative Appendix E.2 is absent. Existing architecture and actionability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Beyond the runtime error bars already present in v1, Appendix I.3/Table 7 adds standard deviations for quality metrics across the five original datasets and multiple-counterfactual methods. These are within-instance counterfactual standard deviations averaged over the test set, not variation across independent training runs. Hypervolume is excluded; no seed counts or confidence intervals are added.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, architecture, masking and runtime values are retained, while Tables 3, 7 and 8 add sensitivity, variability and German Credit results. German Credit validity is 1.000 for both DiCoFlex settings versus 0.954 for DiCE. Some new Adult endpoint values differ from retained Table 1: p=0.01 hypervolume is 0.9023 versus 0.379. Unexplained conditions prevent interpreting this as a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: New Appendix A introduces an expectation/total-variation lemma, a diversity-preservation theorem with separation, KL-convergence and bounded-support assumptions, and propositions with proofs for validity, proximity and plausibility. v1 contains no corresponding formal guarantees. Its introductory scoring definition in Equation (6) is also removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory practical contributions remain substantially unchanged, but the conclusion newly claims rigorous guarantees for validity, proximity, in-distribution plausibility and diversity preservation. This adds a substantive theoretical contribution beyond v1's empirical effectiveness claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds specific limitations concerning model extraction, demographic bias, absent fairness constraints and label accuracy, including a proposed explanation for partial extraction protection. New discussions connect sampling and flow learning to theoretical guarantees and interpret German Credit results as evidence of applicability with limited data. v1's modality, trade-off and training-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices E.1/G newly disclose Adam with learning rate 10^-4, a 1,000-epoch limit, stopping patience 300, hyperparameter ranges/defaults and context-vector implementation. Section 4 adds a code-access link; hardware specifications were already present. However, E.1 describes Figure 3 as training time although its retained caption and discussion concern counterfactual generation.

R1.justification: Six references are added, covering earlier flow-based counterfactual methods, model-extraction attacks and mathematical background. Section 2 now explicitly acknowledges prior normalizing-flow approaches, while Appendix F discusses extraction research. The overall related-work taxonomy and positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 is streamlined around the existing nearest-neighbor procedure, s-DiCoFlex is renamed DiCoFlex (p=0.01), and the shared-model interpretation is clarified. Author/conference information and acknowledgments are updated. Existing section order and most prose remain; the added scientific sections do not constitute a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The result displays expand substantially through new sensitivity, cross-dataset variability and German Credit tables. Runtime Figures 2/3 are redrawn with revised colors and labels, the author block is compacted, and existing actionability tables are relocated. Retained displays can be matched despite renumbering and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves implementation documentation, variability reporting, empirical coverage and discussion of limitations. However, its new theoretical contribution introduces a substantive error: Equation (18) bounds minimum pairwise distance using the probability of at least two distinct draws, although any repeated pair makes that minimum zero. The new sensitivity table also disagrees with retained Table 1 at matching p labels without explaining conditions, and the promised Appendix E.2 is absent. These benefits and new reliability problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
